## id
CON-INF-CC62854BEC55D3

## label
Major microorganism groups exclude plants

## canonical_key
microbiology.classification.microorganism-groups-exclude-plants

## aliases
Microorganism groups
Plants are not microorganisms

## arabic_label


## arabic_aliases
[clear]

## definition
The major microorganism groups include bacteria, fungi, protozoa, helminths and viruses; plants are not in that microorganism list.

## explicit_objective
Identify plants as outside the closed list of major microorganism groups in the local curriculum.

## pitfalls
Bacteria, viruses and protozoa are each explicitly included in the governed microorganism list; plants are not.

## label
Saprophytes feed on dead organic material

microbiology.saprophytes.dead-organic-matter

## aliases
Saprophyte function
Decomposition of dead organic matter

## arabic_label


## arabic_aliases

## definition
Saprophytes feed on dead animal or plant material and thereby decompose dead organic matter.

## explicit_objective
Recognise decomposition of dead organic matter as the function associated with saprophytes.

Saprophytes are not defined by causing human disease, obligate intracellular replication or antibiotic production.

Scientific names capitalize the genus, not the species

Genus capitalization
Binomial nomenclature capitalization

## arabic_label


## arabic_aliases

## definition
In scientific nomenclature the genus is the first name and is capitalized, while the following species name is not capitalized.

## explicit_objective
Identify the genus as the capitalized part of a scientific binomial name.

The species name follows the genus and is not capitalized; family and class are not the two-name position asked by this item.

# Item

## id
CON-INF-98A3DF2E20880C

## label
Viruses are acellular while bacteria are prokaryotic

## canonical_key
microbiology.classification.viruses-acellular-bacteria-prokaryotic

## aliases
Cellular classification of microorganisms
Viruses acellular and bacteria prokaryotic

## arabic_label


## arabic_aliases
[clear]

## definition
Viruses are acellular agents rather than prokaryotic, eukaryotic or multicellular organisms. Bacteria are the prokaryotic microorganisms among fungi, bacteria, protozoa and algae.

## explicit_objective
Classify viruses as acellular agents. Identify bacteria as prokaryotic microorganisms.

## pitfalls
Viruses are not placed under either cellular branch and therefore are not prokaryotic, eukaryotic or multicellular cells. Fungi, protozoa and algae are eukaryotic groups in this comparison; bacteria are prokaryotic.

classification

# Item

## id
CON-INF-9680A199504CCA

## label
A true nucleus distinguishes eukaryotic from prokaryotic cells

## canonical_key
microbiology.cells.prokaryote-vs-eukaryote-nucleus

## aliases
Prokaryotic versus eukaryotic nucleus
True nucleus distinction

## arabic_label


## arabic_aliases
[clear]

## definition
Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus and nuclear membrane, whereas eukaryotic cells have a true membrane-bound nucleus.

## explicit_objective
Use the presence of a true membrane-bound nucleus to distinguish eukaryotic from prokaryotic cells.

## pitfalls
A cell wall is not the universal separator in the offered comparison, and both cell types can reproduce.
